source.title: Do Latent Channels Actually Communicate? A Causal Audit of Latent Multi-Agent LLM Communication
source.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.AI; carries an AAAI copyright notice)

confidence_rationale: PREPRINT (arXiv 2607.26773, 29 Jul 2026; the PDF carries a 'Copyright 2027, AAAI' notice, so it may be accepted to AAAI-27 but that is unverified). Full PDF read. An independent second audit with the same logic as Cheng/Das/Ramnath, on LatentMAS with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B: four message settings (no message; other-example message from the same interface, length-matched; compute-matched self-generated message; current-example message) support five measurements separating message presence, message identity, example-specific content and other-agent value. Headline decomposition verified verbatim: on GSM8K the Qwen3-4B overall effect of -1.00 pp 'decomposes into a -6.17-point effect retained by an other-example message and a +5.17-point effect attributable to example-specific content; both component directions reverse at 8B'; on MATH-500 the 4B gain of 15.00 points is 8.33 retained by an other-example message and 6.67 example-specific. 0.68: preprint, small n (60-100 per cell), and it corroborates rather than adds to Cheng et al. -- but two groups reaching the same decomposition independently is what makes INV-105's control clause a standard rather than one paper's preference.
failure_signatures: INV-105: a net-zero aggregate effect (-1.00 pp) concealed a -6.17 generic-channel component and a +5.17 example-specific component -- so a REE interface experiment reading a null aggregate as 'no transmission' would be wrong in exactly the way this audit exposes, and the sign of each component flipped between 4B and 8B.

Example-specific content and other-agent value are shown to be distinct (self-substitution control): a receiver can benefit from its OWN example-specific latent as much as from another agent's, so 'the sender helped' needs a self-generated comparator, not only a mismatched one.

mapping.source_claim_statement: 'End-task performance alone cannot reveal whether an observed effect depends on message presence, content generated for the evaluated example, or information supplied by a separate agent.' A causal audit applying controlled message replacements at the sender-receiver boundary decomposes latent-relay effects; on GSM8K (Qwen3-4B) -1.00 = -6.17 (other-example) + 5.17 (example-specific) pp, on MATH-500 +15.00 = 8.33 + 6.67, with component directions reversing at 8B. 'Self-substitution comparisons further show that example-specific content and other-agent value are distinct.' Conclusion: controlled message comparisons should be a standard evaluation.
mapping.ree_translation: INV-105's ladder separates 'causally used', 'pairing-specific' and 'behaviourally beneficial', and mandates mismatched-pair controls; this audit adds a further separation REE should adopt -- a compute-matched SELF-generated message -- because example-specific content can come from the receiver's own computation, so 'the other system supplied it' is a rung of its own. The generic-versus-specific decomposition with sign reversals across scale is the strongest available demonstration that an aggregate delta is uninterpretable on its own.
mapping.mapping_caveat: LLM latent relay on maths benchmarks; small per-cell n (40-100), single seed for many cells, one released system (LatentMAS). The transferred content is the decomposition logic and the extra self-substitution control, not any magnitude. Preprint; AAAI acceptance unverified.
mapping.source_context: LLM multi-agent; LatentMAS hidden-state relay; Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B; GSM8K, ARC-C, MATH-500.

confidence_components.notes: Preprint, smaller and less pre-registered than Cheng et al., but methodologically aligned and independent. Mapping fidelity high for the same reason: the audit's decomposition is the ladder.
